policy.statement: Every external source below starts dark: "active": false. Nothing in apps/assistant-api calls one until a deliberate edit flips a single source's flag, with the licence, rate limit and POPIA cross-border position reviewed and recorded first. The adapters in apps/assistant-api/src/lib/sources refuse to operate while their source is dark, so an accident of wiring cannot spend data or reputation either.
policy.activationRequires: 1) A recorded decision against the source's licence and the POPIA s72 cross-border position; 2) credentials, where the source needs any, set in the deployment environment and never in this file; 3) one deliberate commit editing that source's "active" to true.
policy.popiaNote: No patient identifiers are ever sent to an external source: a federated lookup carries only the topic words of a question. Even so, activation stays gated on a recorded cross-border transfer assessment, because a topic can be personal in context.

evidenceGrades.guideline: Clinical or public-health guidance issued by a named authority — SA NDoH, WHO, NICD, SAHPRA, or a professional society whose guidance the catalogue cites.
evidenceGrades.regulatory-label: Wording drawn from a regulator's product label, paired with its South African treatment-guideline counterpart (the drug-interaction entries: OpenFDA / SA NDoH Standard Treatment Guidelines).
evidenceGrades.not-assessed: Service navigation, programme or directory information carried for completeness — no clinical evidence assessment has been performed on the entry, and none is implied.

abstention.no-evidence: MyThuso's approved knowledge base has nothing that speaks to this question. Rather than guess, it says so plainly — a nurse or doctor can help where the records cannot.
abstention.expired-evidence: The record for this topic is past its review date, so it may no longer be current. MyThuso will not present it as fact — please confirm with a nurse, doctor or pharmacist.
abstention.conflicting-evidence: The records for this topic disagree with each other. Where the evidence conflicts, MyThuso does not choose a side for you — a nurse or doctor can weigh it up against your own situation.
abstention.outside-approved-scope: This question falls outside what MyThuso's knowledge base is approved to answer. It is deliberately left unanswered rather than guessed at — please take it to a nurse or doctor.

approved: South African public health system navigation
excluded: anything that needs a licence to interpret (for example radiology or pathology results)
scope.statement: The outside-approved-scope abstention is enforced where an answer is composed for a person — the federation answer path in apps/assistant-api/src/lib/knowledge-federation.ts (federatedSearch, through outsideApprovedScope), which decides scope before any lookup and abstains rather than guessing. That path stays dark until a live route is deliberately wired to it, so today the abstention is a property of answer composition, not of a connected route. The built /assistant/v1/knowledge/search route does not compose an answer at all: it lists the catalogue's own published sources (each id, title and source) through retrieveKnowledge and withholds any match with no source — its no-source-no-fact refusal — so it never returns a diagnosis for the abstention to catch, and the frozen knowledge/search@2 contract declares no outside-approved-scope refusal.

sources.name: WHO International Classification of Diseases 11th Revision (ICD-11) API
sources.activation: Requires an ICD API client registered with WHO (client id and secret set in the deployment environment as ICD11_CLIENT_ID and ICD11_CLIENT_SECRET), a recorded licence and POPIA review, and this flag edited to true.

rateLimit.basis: Self-imposed ceiling. WHO does not publish a fixed public rate limit for the ICD API; a registered client's quota is confirmed with WHO ICD Access Management at registration, and this ceiling stays below it.

licensing.notes: ICD-11 is WHO copyright, licensed CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO: no derivatives. ICD-11 content would be presented unmodified and attributed, never folded into an edited derivative.

dataResidency.notes: A lookup sends only the topic words of a question, never a patient identifier; the request still crosses the border, so activation waits on a recorded POPIA s72 assessment.

sources.useFor: Validating and enriching the terminology codes the catalogue maps to its own entries.
sources.notFor: Clinical decision support, diagnosis lookup on behalf of a patient, or answering a person's question directly.

sources.name: openFDA drug label API (US Food and Drug Administration)
sources.activation: Optional free API key in the deployment environment as OPENFDA_API_KEY (the API works without one at the lower public limits), a recorded licence and POPIA review, and this flag edited to true.

auth.notes: No key is required; an optional key raises the daily ceiling from 1,000 to 120,000 requests.

rateLimit.basis: openFDA's documented unauthenticated limits (open.fda.gov/apis/authentication): 240 requests per minute and 1,000 per day per IP address; with an API key the daily ceiling rises to 120,000.

licensing.notes: openFDA data is a public-domain US Government dataset; MyThuso would still record its origin on every result, because attribution is a habit, not a requirement.

dataResidency.notes: A lookup sends a medicine's generic name, never a patient; the request still crosses the border, so activation waits on a recorded POPIA s72 assessment.

sources.useFor: Checking the catalogue's recorded drug-interaction warnings against the regulator's own label text.
sources.notFor: Presenting US label wording to a South African patient as though it were SA guidance without the SA NDoH treatment-guideline line beside it, or any dose, diagnosis or prescribing answer.

sources.name: Europe PMC REST search (PubMed and PMC literature)
sources.activation: No credentials required; activation needs a recorded licence and POPIA review and this flag edited to true.

auth.notes: No credentials; a descriptive User-Agent identifies the deployment, the same politeness the literature_search tool already practises.

rateLimit.basis: Self-imposed ceiling — Europe PMC publishes no fixed request-rate limit, so this deployment stays deliberately slow rather than testing any limit there may be.

licensing.notes: Metadata and abstracts are served by Europe PMC; each article's full text keeps its own licence (CC BY, CC BY-NC or publisher terms), so only identifiers, titles and abstract openings would ever be carried, each attributed to its journal.

dataResidency.notes: A lookup sends only a topic string, never a patient; the request still crosses the border, so activation waits on a recorded POPIA s72 assessment.

sources.useFor: Finding published literature that speaks to a question, always by a checkable identifier, the same discipline the literature_search tool already follows.
sources.notFor: Treating a search hit as clinical evidence by itself, or carrying any conclusion beyond the paper's own title and abstract opening.
